subject: Oceanography
title: Coral Restoration
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Coral Restoration.

hook.text: Scientists are growing corals in underwater nurseries—then transplanting them to damaged reefs.

buildup.text: Coral fragments are attached to 'trees' or tables—growing 5–10 times faster than on natural reefs.

discovery.text: Selective breeding and assisted evolution aim to create heat-resistant coral strains—'super corals.'

twist.text: Restoration alone can't save reefs—if ocean warming continues, transplanted corals will bleach too.

climax.text: The real bottleneck is scale—we've restored hundreds of hectares, but reefs span hundreds of thousands.

punchline.text: We can grow corals faster—but not faster than warming kills them.

quiz.question: What is the main challenge for coral restoration?
options: Scale—restored areas are tiny compared to total reef area needing help
